rationale: HeadlessSurface is used for executable pixel proof, but Dawn can initialize its Null backend on a host with no native GPU driver. That backend accepts rendering commands yet produces a flat zero-variance readback, so treating it as a successful capture would turn unavailable hardware into false product evidence. The Pulp-owned headless wrapper now rejects unavailable and Null adapters before Skia setup, allowing callers to take the existing explicit runtime-skip path while retaining real proof on a native GPU. This is a Pulp-only evidence-integrity guard; it does not change Vellum framework behavior or the public rendering API.
tests: AudioInspectorPanel renders a non-empty headless snapshot
